# Final Review Proposal
**Producer:** agent:codex/gpt-5.4

## Summary

Reviewed the budget-ledger/helpers, engine guard, and touched mass-routing systems. I found two correctness issues: the shrimp reserve introduced by the routing changes is never spent for hatching/maturation and now breaks the population-growth path, and the new per-tick guard stops checking for unexplained drift on any tick that includes an open-system action.

## Amendments

1. crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:230-235,443-446,530-533,626-656 and crates/tank_core/src/types/biology.rs:85-91: the new hatching/maturation funding path pulls biomass from dissolved water pools even though feeding explicitly routes the retained share into animal.reserve_g and documents that reserve as the store used for growth/reproduction. reserve_g is never debited, so retained mass becomes a dead-end pool while successful hatches/maturation depend on DON/TAN/DOC/DIC instead of stored food. This is already visible in crates/tank_core/tests/shrimp_population.rs:103-117: cargo test -p tank_core --test shrimp_population hatch_produces_juveniles now fails under the "good conditions" fixture. Hatching and juvenile maturation should spend reserve_g (or reserve first, then water if that is the intended model) rather than bypassing it.
   Rationale: This is a shipping regression in core shrimp lifecycle behavior, and it directly contradicts the retained-reserve contract introduced by the change.
2. crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:524-545 and 563-600: the tracked-budget guard is disabled wholesale whenever a tick contains any non-zero action:feed/action:water_change/action:siphon_detritus/action:add_shrimp/action:remove_shrimp flux. That means a tick with a legitimate open-system action and an unrelated leak later in the hour will never raise BudgetImbalance; the action delta masks the rest of the tick instead of being subtracted from the residual. You already do the right residual-based subtraction for chemistry carbon at crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:577-589. Apply the same pattern to open-system action fluxes so mixed ticks still detect unexplained nitrogen/carbon drift.
   Rationale: As written, the new conservation guard is only trustworthy on action-free ticks. Common debugging cases like water changes and feed events can still hide real leaks, which weakens the main value of the ledger/guard instrumentation.
